title: Platform routing & quota blitz — standup notes
body:
Attendees: Asha, Miguel, Lena, Rafiq, Maya, Tom (SRE)

Meeting objective: quick sync to triage the quota-throttling regression seen yesterday, align on routing fallback that dropped auth header in canary, and set owners for the quota redesign spike. Keep this light — action-driven.

TL;DR
- Incident yesterday: transient spike in 401s for a small set of customers (0.4% of traffic) between 03:12–03:40UTC; root cause traced to a quota refresh race + routing fallback that re-issued requests without auth header.
- Short-term mitigation: revert allocator change in PR 762 rolled out to canary; enable strict header-preserve policy for fallback proxy; push emergency rate limiter config change (increase throttle-window to 5s) — deployed 04:10UTC and errors dropped to baseline.
- Long-term: approved spike to redesign per-tenant quota cache + leaky-bucket refactor to remove refresh races (owner: Miguel, due: 2026-08-05).

Notes + timeline (raw)
- 03:08UTC - alert: quota-throttle rate up on svc-hosted-route-3, spike in token-bucket rejects.
- 03:12 - SRE paged platform oncall; error budget alerts triggered for 3 customers.
- 03:15 - initial rollback attempt of allocator commit (routed to canary) — false negative, metric noise.
- 03:22 - debug: observed that when allocator failed over to remote pool, the fallback proxy executed a synthetic retry but did not include X-Redwood-Auth header due to a middleware ordering change in proxy v2.1.3. This produced 401s, which in turn triggered quota refresh attempts.
- 03:30 - found concurrent quota refresh transactions causing stale token counts to be double-applied for ~20s windows. Race reproduced locally with stress harness (thanks Rafiq).
- 04:02 - hotfix PR to proxy to preserve headers in synthetic retries created and merged (PR: preserve-retry-headers).
- 04:10 - deployed config change to throttle-window, revert allocator patch on canary. Errors returned to baseline by 04:18.

Impact summary
- User-facing: small set of customers experienced increased failed requests (401) and some requests billed as throttled while actually failing auth; no data exfiltration.
- SLO: short-lived increase in auth failure rate, no sustained SLO breach.
- Billing/Quotas: some invoices may show extra token requests due to retries — ops will run reconciliation script.

Root cause analysis (current hypothesis)
1) Allocator change (PR 762) altered how routing fallback chooses pools — introduced a path where requests were proxied through a retry layer.
2) Proxy middleware ordering change (v2.1.3) caused header-strip on synthetic retries (missing X-Redwood-Auth).
3) Missing auth produced 401 -> client libraries retried -> quota service received refresh requests with incomplete state -> token-bucket refresh race produced double decrements in a small window.

Immediate mitigations (done)
- Revert allocator change on canary and block rollout until spike completes (owner: Lena).
- Hotfix to preserve headers on retry merged and deployed (owner: Tom SRE).
- Temporarily increase throttle-window to 5s cluster-wide to reduce double-refresh sensitivity (owner: Maya).
- Run reconciliation for possible duplicate billed requests (owner: Billing ops, linked JIRA JIRA-PLAT-1392).

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Miguel: Lead the quota-cache + leaky-bucket refactor spike. Draft design doc with sequence diagrams and failure modes. Due 2026-08-05. (Confluence: Quota Design Spike 2026)
- Lena: Hold allocator patch (PR 762) until the spike validates no regressions; set canary gate. Due: 2026-08-01.
- Rafiq: Finish stress harness reproducer and share steps + a minimal repro script in repo (allocator/test/stress). Due: 2026-07-27.
- Tom (SRE): Add a synthetic test in staging that verifies header preservation on retries and fails the build on regression. Due: 2026-07-29.
- Maya: Coordinate with Billing to run reconciliation job and ensure affected customers notified if necessary; prepare draft support message. Due: 2026-07-24.
- Asha: Run a short postmortem note and share with leadership + ops. Due: 2026-07-25.

Design notes for spike (brain dump)
- Problem: current quota service uses an optimistic refresh pattern that assumes single-writer per tenant; under concurrent refreshes we see double-applies. Need a design that:
  - makes refresh idempotent (operation ids / vector clocks) OR
  - migrates to a central ledger with compare-and-swap semantics for counters OR
  - uses local per-proxy delta aggregation + periodic reconciliation to central store.
- Tradeoffs to consider: latency impact of CAS vs. eventual errors, cost of cross-AZ locks, complexity of migration.
- Proposal A (fast): add operation-id-based idempotency for refresh calls + small TTLed cache of recent ops per-tenant on quota service.
- Proposal B (robust): move to per-tenant sequence numbers maintained in redis with WATCH/TRANSACTION for atomic updates. Potential hotspots — may need sharding.
- Proposal C (architectural): extend runtime allocator to avoid synthetic retries for auth failures; prefer transparent error propagation to client and local backoff.

Testing and rollout plan ideas
- Create a canary suite that simulates high-concurrency quota refresh + auth retry pattern. Run in staging with 10x normal concurrency.
- Add a synthetic regression test for header-preserve in proxy (blocking).
- Feature-flag the new quota idempotency behavior; initial rollout to small tenants (10 customers) with deep telemetry.
- If CAS-based approach selected, do phased migration by tenant ranges and monitor token-consumption deltas.

Discussion snippets (raw)
- Miguel: "Prefer A as fastest path to stop races; B only if A proves insufficient in load tests."
- Lena: "Allocator change needs additional invariants — we accidentally created a retry path that is safe in most cases but not for auth flows."
- Rafiq: "I can push the repro harness today, it's just parameter tuning. We found the race at ~300 concurrent refreshes per tenant in local sim."
- Maya: "Billing ops will want a precise list of request-ids to reconcile; please ensure logs contain X-Request-Id and quota-op-id in the retry path."

Open questions / risks
- If we only add idempotency cache, what's the worst memory/SSD footprint per tenant? (Miguel to estimate)
- Will CAS/redis WATCH scale under our tenant distribution? Need perf numbers (Tom).
- Any GDPR/PII concerns with storing extra op metadata? (legal check with Security & Compliance)
- Potential for prolonged partial degradation if allocator patch is rolled back incompletely. (Lena)

Housekeeping & next steps
- Quick follow-up meeting Friday 2026-07-24 09:30PT — 30m. Objective: review Miguel's draft design and the repro harness output.
- Miguel to create Confluence page (linked above) and attach sequence diagrams + failure injection plan.
- Rafiq to open a test-only PR that adds the stress harness and a README for running locally.
- Lena to add a canary gate in the allocator pipeline and add checklist items for header-preserve validation.

Appendix: Useful links / artifacts
- Repro harness: github: allocator/tests/stress/repro-2026-07
- Hotfix PR (proxy header preserve): github: redwood-inference/proxy/PR-1184 (merged)
- Allocator revert PR: github: redwood-inference/allocator/PR-763 (revert)
- Incident thread: slack #plat-routing (thread ts 1711071000.000200)

Notes to self (ASAP)
- Add telemetry: quota-op-id in request logs, increase retention for the next 72h in staging.
- Confirm that billing reconciliation excludes failed-auth retries (edge-case).

End of notes.

Raw/rough — will polish into postmortem after Miguel's design and Rafiq's repro are in place.
